Outgoing webhooks misbehave when a workspace admin switches an endpoint off in the webhook settings (seen on a Growth-plan workspace, which includes webhooks and up to 10 endpoints):

1. Switching an endpoint off looks like it saved, but the endpoint comes back still switched on, and new events (for example a newly created issue) keep being queued for it. Switching an endpoint off must stick, switching it back on must work too, and while it is off no new deliveries may be queued for it.
2. Events that were queued for an endpoint before it was switched off still go out on the next delivery run. When the delivery run reaches a queued delivery whose endpoint is switched off (or no longer exists), that delivery must be marked failed instead of delivered. Deliveries for endpoints that are still on must keep being delivered, and the run must keep counting delivered and failed deliveries as before.
3. A switched-off endpoint must keep counting toward the plan's endpoint allowance. Currently the check made when creating an endpoint ignores switched-off endpoints, so a workspace that already has as many endpoints as its plan allows could create another one just by switching one off first. That must be refused, exactly as when all endpoints are on.
